summary: Pacific County WA tower site: 20-ft L-4 tower 1947, lost 1953 to storm or fire (sources differ), replacement abandoned 1967; no standing structure described.

facts.design: 20-foot wooden tower with L-4 cab (the replacement tower, 1953)
facts.status_note: Replacement tower abandoned in 1967 and since removed or probably destroyed; sources differ

access.note: Reached by a DNR road that Willhite calls well traveled and built for any vehicle; no gate or closure mentioned

visit.trail_note: Drive to a parking area, then an old road uphill into the timber; Willhite lists a quarter mile and 100 feet of gain

events.note: 20-foot wooden L-4 tower; firetower.org says it burned by accident
Tower named Cowan Peak; announced as run cooperatively by the association, the State Division of Forestry and Weyerhaeuser
January 1953 storm; Willhite and a February 1953 Longview newspaper say it was demolished by the storm
Replacement 20-foot tower with L-4 cab, built later in 1953; named for Major Charles S. Cowan
Lookout William F. Glover, 21, died at his station, overcome by heating gas (Daily Chronicle)
Replacement tower abandoned; firetower.org says since removed, others say probably destroyed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firetower.org says the 1947 tower burned by accident. Willhite and a February 1953 Longview newspaper report say the January 1953 storm demolished it. The story reports both.
Firetower.org says it has since been removed; FireLookout.com and Willhite say it was probably destroyed soon after its 1967 abandonment. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Brief names the site Cowan Point; Willhite and the Washington Lookouts page use Cowan Peak, so both names are given. Storm-versus-fire account of the 1947 tower conflicts across sources and is reported as a conflict. Glover's 1959 death is included as staffing history and kept brief. Willhite's route page gives no visit date, so the footings are not dated.
